title: What If the Air Had 35 Percent Oxygen Instead of 21?

scenes.text: What if air held 35 percent oxygen, not 21? Earth once may have.
In the Carboniferous, estimates put oxygen at 30 to 35 percent, compared with about 21 today.
Back then, dragonfly-like insects called Meganeura had wingspans of about two feet, nearly a crow's.
Insects breathe through tubes instead of lungs, so more oxygen may let them grow bigger.
The link is not proven. Researchers compiled over 10,000 fossil records, and wingspans rose and fell with oxygen.
Today's biggest dragonfly spans about six inches. Richer air might have made bugs the size of birds.
